title: Quick Revision: Light – Reflection and Refraction
subject: Science

table: Power P = 1/f (f in metres), unit dioptre (D)

blocks.p: **New Cartesian convention:** distances are measured from the pole or optical centre. Object on the left, so u is always negative. Distances along the incident light are +, against it are –. Heights above the axis are +, below are –. **Negative m = real and inverted. Positive m = virtual and erect.**
**Convex mirror** and **concave lens** always give a virtual, erect, diminished image (convex mirror: behind the mirror between P and F; concave lens: between F_{1} and O).

bullets: Light bends because its speed changes. Going into a denser medium (air → glass) it bends **towards** the normal; going into a rarer medium it bends away.
Laws: incident ray, refracted ray and normal lie in one plane; **sin i / sin r = constant** (Snell's law).
Refractive index n = c/v (speed in vacuum ÷ speed in medium). n_{21} = v_{1}/v_{2}. Glass slab: the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways.
Values to remember: water 1.33, kerosene 1.44, crown glass 1.52, diamond 2.42 (optically densest).

box: **Uses.** Concave mirror: torches and headlights, shaving and dentists' mirrors, solar furnaces. Convex mirror: rear-view mirrors (erect image, wider view).

**Ray-diagram rules:** a ray parallel to the axis passes through (or appears to come from) F; a ray through F becomes parallel; a ray through C (mirror) returns along itself; a ray through O (lens) goes straight.

blocks.p: 1. Power of a lens is –2.5 D. What is its focal length, and what type of lens is it?
2. Where should an object be placed in front of a concave mirror to get a same-size real image?
